title: Reward-to-risk
desc: Why a 2:1 trade can pay even when you’re wrong most of the time

cards.title: Which setup pays?
cards.situation: You win 4 trades out of 10. Setup A risks $2 to make $2. Setup B risks $2 to make $6. Which one pays over time?

options.feedback: At 1:1 you need to win more than half your trades. At 40%, A slowly loses.
B’s wins are three times its losses. That pays even when you’re wrong 6 times in 10.

options.text: Both the same: you win 40% either way
options.feedback: Same win rate, different payoffs. What each win pays compared with each loss decides the result.

cards.title: Reward-to-risk
cards.text: Compare what you could make with what you could lose. Pros aim for **2:1 or more**: at least $2 of reward for every $1 of risk.

visual.title: Trade plan
visual.label: Entry $50, stop $48, target $54: risk $2 to make $4

cards.title: Right less than half the time
cards.text: The better the [[reward-to-risk|reward-to-risk]], the fewer trades you need to win just to break even.

rows.note: Win $1, lose $1: you need a win for every loss.
One $2 win covers two $1 losses: 1 win in 3.
One $3 win covers three $1 losses: 1 win in 4.

cards.title: The target has to be real
cards.text: A 5:1 plan means nothing if the target sits **past resistance** that price keeps failing at. Put the target just before the next ceiling. If 2:1 doesn’t fit, **skip the trade**.

cards.title: Work out the ratio
cards.q: Entry $30, stop $28, target $36. What’s the reward-to-risk?

options.feedback: That’s upside down. Reward goes first: $6 of reward against $2 of risk.
$2 is the risk, not the ratio. Divide the $6 reward by it.
$6 of reward for $2 of risk: three dollars for every one you put on the line.
$6 is the reward. Divide it by the $2 risk.

cards.title: Win rate 40%
cards.q: You win about 4 trades in 10. Which reward-to-risk can keep you profitable over time, before fees?

options.feedback: At 1:1 you need to win over 50%. At 2:1, 40% is enough: 4 × $2 − 6 × $1 = +$2.
At 2:1 you break even at about 33%, so 40% wins pays: 4 × $2 − 6 × $1 = +$2.
At 1:2 each win is half a loss. You’d need to win about two trades in three.
It matters a lot. With 40% wins, only a reward bigger than the risk keeps you ahead.

cards.headline: You can tell if a trade is worth taking.
lines: At 2:1 you can be right less than half the time.
